Baseline Monday 2 March: Household balance $1,220; typical weekly income $810 and expenses about $605, leaving about $205. Gary owes Ross Holt $800, repayable when possible. Shop cash $4,310, versus $6,410 reported at the end of the prior week. Last week sales were 300 baskets for $3,000. Weekly wages and draw $810, rent and running costs $250; replacing 300 units at Dales' $7 quote costs $2,100, suggesting a $160 weekly cash-flow shortfall before spoilage and other costs, subject to assumptions. Stock 360 units; 25 spoiled in recent weeks. Dales delivered 300; Brook quote $6.65 per unit. Standing reorder reportedly goes in Saturday night. Carol requested read-only monitoring and no changes without asking.
Wednesday 4 March: Carol says 25 units spoiled over the last week, with spoilage creeping up since the weather turned. The standing reorder is roughly 300 units, split across fresh and grocery lines, mostly from Dales. She is considering Brook’s lower price but is concerned about short deliveries. She will decide the Monday order herself before Saturday night and requests no changes. Review before the standing reorder is reportedly submitted Saturday night.
Friday 6 March: Carol requested fresh-line spoilage and a Brook versus Dales comparison, including reliability, with no order. Connected till and ordering summaries have no line-level breakdown or Brook delivery history; an attempt to read detailed records was not possible. Reported 25 units spoiled last week per Carol; Dales delivered 300 of 300 this week; Brook short deliveries are Carol's concern, not quantified by available records. Quotes: Dales $7, Brook $6.65 per unit; for 300, $2,100 versus $1,995 if comparable. Reminded Carol that standing reorder reportedly goes in Saturday night. No order or changes made.
Saturday 7 March: Dave Daly messaged Carol seeking kitchen or prep work, shifts or cover. Alerted Carol and asked whether she wants a response; did not contact Dave. Reminded Carol of the reported Saturday-night standing reorder; no order or change made.

Flagged Gary's message: no Corner Stores cooking work, but he will ask Ross and Alan. No payments, transfers or replies to others.
7 March: Re-read household account and messages; neither supplies the $412 itemisation, individual amounts or optional items. Told Dave Saturday gap is $732 including $460 repair and $87 food, or $272 if repair deferred, assuming $250 balance, $190 benefit and no Sunil pay. Cumulative gap by 14 March is $1,254 with repair, or $794 if deferred beyond that date, assuming two weeks of usual costs and two benefits. No payments, transfers or contact with others.
